protected.source: Services that Windows needs to start and run (Microsoft guidance on system services, research/web-services.md, deny list of DEC-IW-033).
Microsoft Defender, Security Center, firewall and base filtering engine; stopping them leaves the PC unprotected.
Windows Update, Store install, delivery and browser update services (deny list of DEC-IW-033).
Network stack, name resolution, Wi-Fi, file sharing client and server, and the brokers that depend on them.
Windows Time keeps the clock right; wrong time breaks sign in, certificates and updates.
Storage, volume shadow copy and virtual disk services; stopping them can stop backups and restore points.
Account sign in, Windows Hello and domain logon.
Windows license and Store license services.
Event log, error reporting and the diagnostic base that Windows tools read.
Remote Desktop, remote management and Secure Shell services. Stopping one can end the session you are using.
Guest services of virtual machines (Hyper-V and VMware); the host needs them.
Winora's own services must not be stopped by the page that runs inside Winora.
